name: Combat
subtitle: Centered on trading and countering with opponents and skills; the core revolves around windows, resources, and reading moves.
demoRuleHint: Rule: Observe opponent → Choose skill → Resolve (hit/block/evade) → Feedback (damage/stagger) → Resource recovery
problemsSolved: Clarify attack/defense windows (wind-up/active/stagger) to reduce 'unfair hits'.
Use resources (stamina/cooldown/distance) to constrain skill usage, forcing choices and rhythm.
Balance hit weight and risk/reward so that 'attack/evade/block' each carry value.

Balance wind‑up length and rhythm: a too‑short wind‑up allows combos but removes counter windows; a too‑long wind‑up is easy to interrupt but allows move reading. Designers must balance combo fluidity with defensive readability.
Resource recovery speed versus skill variety: too fast recovery leads to mindless skill loops; too slow limits combo depth, increasing strategic depth.
learningGoals: Beginner: understand the attack/defense loop — observe → strike → judge → feedback → resource regen — and reproduce one attack and one block in the demo
Intermediate: write the window contract (wind-up / block window / hit-stun) and the resource contract (stamina/cooldown spend and regen)
Advanced: design move-counter relationships and counterplay space, and verify balance with exchange ratio, block rate, and mash frequency
minimalRules: Actions: the player may choose to attack, block, or move; attacks require a wind‑up window; movement requires a movement window.

Resolution: hit chance is based on accuracy + opponent's evasion; if accuracy > evasion, it's a hit; block chance is based on block rate + opponent's attack power; if block rate > attack power, it's a block.
Invincibility check: if a skill's invincibility frames exceed the opponent's action duration, the opponent cannot be hit.
Resources: stamina/cooldown; attacks consume stamina/cooldown; movement consumes stamina; blocking consumes stamina.
Windows: wind‑up, block window, movement window, stagger window; each window length is configurable.
systemLoopHint: Input (skill selection) → Resolve (hit/counter) → Feedback (damage/stagger) → Resource change (cooldown/stamina) → New window → New input

combos.effect: Use matches to trigger skills and rhythm points
Add building/selection, allowing mid‑to‑long‑term decisions to influence the confrontation

advancedWarnings: Unclear wind‑ups render counters ineffective, turning combat into a numbers game.
Too fast resource recovery leads to mindless skill loops.
Missing stagger/recoil removes weight from hits.
Shorter wind‑ups increase overall pace but may shrink defensive space, forcing players into passive attacks and counterintuitively lowering the experience.
advancedAlgoRefs: State Machine: skill states, cancellation, stagger, hit
Hit Detection: colliders, invincibility frames, combo windows

demoLab.title: Resource Exchange Experiment
demoLab.action: Spam "Attack (primary)" until stamina bottoms out, watching hits and damage change
demoLab.observe: Stamina is the attack budget: once empty, attacks whiff and you are forced into a regen window. The resource constraint forces a fight/rest rhythm — the cost of button mashing made explicit

demoLab.title: Block Window Experiment
demoLab.action: As the enemy closes in, switch to "Block (secondary)" and watch guard and hp trade off
demoLab.observe: Blocking converts damage into guard drain: defense is not immunity but resource substitution. Once guard runs out, further blocks fail — the defensive window has its own budget, capping the turtle strategy

demoLab.title: Difficulty Contrast
demoLab.action: On easy vs hard, "Advance 1 Step" 10 steps each and compare the hp drain curves
demoLab.observe: On hard, enemyHp is thicker and enemy attacks more frequent — same attack loop, completely different hp slope. Difficulty is fundamentally an adjustment of the exchange ratio: each of your hits buys less enemy health

intro.what: Trade blows with an opponent up close — when your health bar empties, you lose. Fighting games and action-game boss fights are built on this.
intro.feel: You read the opponent’s wind-up, strike into the gap; when stamina runs dry you retreat while gasping — every hit lands with weight, every block is a held breath.
intro.why: An introductory dissection of "the dueling feel" — once windows, resources, and move-reading click, every confrontation design has its skeleton.

concept: Combat play translates "conflict" into readable exchanges: attacks have wind-ups, defenses have windows, resources have budgets — every strike settles risk against reward on the spot. The hard part is not the move count — it is the explainability of the exchange: unclear wind-ups kill counterplay, too-fast resource regen turns skills into mindless loops, and missing hit-stun robs impacts of weight. Players feel "that was a fair fight" because wins and losses both trace back to specific reads and choices.
designNotes: Defense is not immunity — it is resource substitution: blocking converts health loss into guard-resource drain, so the turtle strategy caps itself at the defense budget without any extra ban.

Shorter wind-ups can make the game worse (counterintuitive): faster moves smooth out combos but compress the defender’s read window, degrading the duel into a pure speed contest — pace may only improve if counterplay space survives.

Hit-stun and knockback are the "weight" of a hit: players feel nothing from number decrements — it is the flinch and displacement that say "that landed." Without them, combat becomes two health bars being picked at.
